title: A theoretical and methodological proposal for M-Self: an identity-activation and cross-role transfer protocol for life transitions
abstract: Life transitions can compress the working self into a single salient identity, muting resources from other roles. The Identity Activation and Cross-Role Transfer protocol (MSelf) is a brief, modular protocol that maps roles to traits and emotions, translates traits into Universal Behaviours (UBs), and rehearses small, situated cross-role transfers; an optional light-touch heart rate variability (HRV) and electroencephalography (EEG) layer provides formative state feedback. Pragmatic implementations in four cohorts: maternity return-to-work (11,527 mothers reached; 2024 mixed-audience survey n = 715), women nearing release from prison (N = 12), young-women mentorship (analytic N = 500; programme enrolment = 555), and an eating-disorder programme (N = 85), show within-person pre-post signals of higher self-efficacy and transfer frequency and lower perceived stress. Making identity complexity visible and transfer feasible may convert transitions into developmental opportunities. Evidence is exploratory, nonrandomized, and largely self-reported; randomized and longitudinal studies are needed.
